expectations.text: Names explicit EXCLUSIONS by directory or file type (e.g. node_modules, .venv, archive, binaries, test fixtures)
expectations.evidence: Only exclusion named is by ExecStart type ('roughly 56 of the ~240 ExecStart lines are NOT Python ... goose-d2m run --recipe ...yaml, ttyd'). No directory-based or file-type exclusions (.venv, node_modules, archive, binaries, test fixtures) are named anywhere in the spec.

expectations.text: Instructs the follower where to start (a cd or explicit working directory)
expectations.evidence: Step 1 says 'Enumerate every unit: ls ~/.config/systemd/user/*.timer' — an enumeration command, but there is no explicit 'cd into X' or working-directory statement anywhere in the spec.

expectations.text: Acceptance criteria are shell-checkable commands whose output decides pass/fail without interpretation
expectations.evidence: Criteria are prose descriptions requiring human judgment, e.g. 'Spot-check pass rate ≥ 90%: pull a random 20-script sample ... independently re-read those 20 scripts, and confirm the verdict matches' — this requires a human/LLM to re-read and judge, not a shell command whose output alone decides pass/fail.

expectations.text: Acceptance criteria constrain the SUBJECT/scope of the audit, not only the output schema
expectations.evidence: Criterion 4: 'Exclusion list matches the filter: spot-check 5 excluded entries against their actual ExecStart lines — confirm none of them are secretly Python' checks that scope/subject was applied correctly, not just output shape.

expectations.text: Warns that schema-only criteria can be satisfied by work that ignored the scope
expectations.evidence: No statement anywhere in the document warns that a follower could satisfy schema-shaped criteria (row count, verdict enum, evidence column) while having audited the wrong scope.
